Subject: Clearwell Health DPIA template & evidence request

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. Attached is our standard DPIA template (v2) — we use this for all vendors that process patient-identifiable or pseudonymised health records. Would Redwood be able to complete the template and return it along with any supporting evidence (SOC 2, data flow diagrams, list of subprocessors and retention policy excerpts) by end of next week (2026-03-15)?

A few specific areas we're focusing on:
- Data categories and lawful basis for processing
- Cross-border transfers and SCCs
- Data minimization and retention controls
- Technical measures for pseudonymisation and encryption (at-rest and in-transit)
- Access control and logging (audit trails)
- Any DPIA risk scoring you apply and mitigations for high-risk processing

If it's easier, we can take a short (30-min) walkthrough after you return the template — happy to coordinate calendars.

Best,
Amelia Ford
DPO, Clearwell Health

Hi Amelia — thanks for sending this over and for the clear priorities. We're able to take this on and will aim to return the completed template plus evidence by 2026-03-15. Quick clarifications so we give precisely what you need:

1) Scope: will the template cover only Redwood-hosted inference (hosted API) usage, or do you also want details for Dedicated/Private options in case Clearwell ever requests a VPC/on-prem deployment?
2) Subprocessors: do you need the full supplier list (tiered with roles), or just those that process customer data (e.g., storage, logging, telemetry) plus any cloud infra providers?
3) Risk scoring: do you have a preferred scale (e.g., Low/Med/High) or a numeric matrix you want us to map to?

Proposed plan: Grace will pull the SOC2 artifact and data flow diagram, Karthik will draft the technical controls section and retention table, and I will complete the DPIA template and do a final review.

If that's acceptable, we'll proceed and share an initial draft in our shared Drive link (I'll include it below) and propose a 30-minute review call early next week if you prefer a run-through.

Thanks — Hannah

Hi Amelia — great, thanks for the quick confirmation. Attached are the initial artifacts we discussed: Redwood_SOC2_Report_Q4_2025.pdf (redacted where needed), a high-level data flow diagram (redwood_data_flow_diagram_v1.png), and our completed responses to the template (we've uploaded the filled spreadsheet to the shared Drive and included answers inline in the template).

Key points we highlighted in the template:
- Lawful basis: Processing is performed under contract performance and legitimate interest for model improvement; we call out processing of Protected Health Information only when customers elect to send PHI and provide contractual safeguards (BAA/contract addendum).
- Transfers: We rely on SCCs for transfers outside the EEA and support customer-requested SCCs; Private/Dedicated options avoid cross-border transfers when required.
- Minimization & retention: Token-level telemetry retained for 14 days by default; request/response logs that are customer-configurable per contract (retention table included).
- Technical controls: TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest for customer data blobs, per-customer key wrapping with KMS for Dedicated/private; pseudonymisation recommendations noted.
- Access & audit: Role-based access, least privilege, mandatory 2FA for console/API access; audit logs retained per contract and surfaced in Console.
- DPIA scoring: We used Low/Medium/High with mitigations mapped to any High items (none flagged as High for hosted API when used with contractual safeguards).

Next steps proposed:
1) You review the attached and flag any gaps by 2026-03-11.
2) If helpful, we can book a 30-minute walkthrough on Tue 2026-03-10 at 10:00 AM PST or Wed 2026-03-11 at 09:00 AM PST — please confirm a slot.
